title: Refactor runtime task topology: isolate slow-IO lanes, add async rehydration worker, remove global-epoch dependency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the past 18 months the continuous-batcher and KV rehydration code paths have accreted several synchronous IO touchpoints and a global epoch coordination primitive. These make the runtime susceptible to head-of-line stalls when an occasional slow disk/IO op or GC spike occurs, and they complicate per-tenant fairness and ownership during model swap/drain.

Objective: Introduce a lightweight handoff fabric and an async rehydration worker so that slow IO does not block the hot fast-path. At the same time, remove the monolithic global-epoch lock and replace it with per-shard lease windows + handoff guarantees. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency tail, simplify reasoning about lease ownership, and unlock safer incremental refactors for session checkpointing.

Scope:
- Implement per-shard handoff queues (bounded, lock-free ring) and a small state machine for safe ownership transfer.
- Introduce an async rehydration worker pool that consumes handoff tasks and performs IO/rehydration without blocking batch lanes.
- Replace the global epoch heartbeat with per-shard lease windows and a best-effort reconciler.
- Add visibility: new telemetry metrics for handoff queue depth, rehydrate latency histogram, and lease transfer events.
- Upgrade async IO dependency (libaio wrapper) to a modern async-io shim requested by infra (see notes).

Non-goals: Full rewrite of batch admission logic; changes to model-level routing policies; major API surface changes. This is an internal runtime topology change only.

Success criteria:
- End-to-end p95 token latency reduced by >=10% on stress workloads with induced IO noise.
- p99 improved (or at least not regressed) on our existing CI benchmarks.
- No increase in error rates or OOM incidents in canary.
- Observability added and used by on-call to triage at least one production incident during rollout.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: subtle race in handoff transfer during shard rebalancing. Mitigation: formalize transfer protocol, add invariant checks and deterministic unit tests.
- Risk: rehydration worker scheduling starves other background tasks. Mitigation: bounded pools + backpressure signals propagated to admission controller.
- Risk: dependency upgrade introduces ABI changes. Mitigation: run staged canaries and wrap the upgrade behind a runtime feature flag.

Testing plan: unit tests for transfer state machine, integration tests with synthetic IO latency injection, bench harness run against model-sim workloads, canary in dedicated cluster with 1% traffic, rollback plan if error rates increase.

Docs & artifacts: PR doc + design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Handoff+Fabric+Design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824, benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/handoff-fabric-canary
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after oncall incident where a single slow NVMe reclaim caused slot allocator stalls for ~18s. Attached initial heap/trace and p95 spike graphs.

2026-03-03 — Marco Nguyen: Did a short spike: implemented a single-threaded async rehydration worker and measured local bench. Observed tail latency improvement for synthetic 5% slow-read noise (p95 down ~12%, p99 down ~6%). Pushed prototype branch runtime/feature/handoff-proto.

2026-03-04 — Lina Morales (code review): Left feedback on transfer protocol: need explicit idempotency token on handoff ACKs to avoid double-apply on reconnect. Also request additional unit tests around duplicate message scenarios.
2026-03-05 — Marco Nguyen: Addressed Lina's feedback, added idempotency tokens and a deterministic state-fuzz tester. Expanded bench harness to simulate staged shard rebalances.

2026-03-06 — Infra (ops): Requested that async-io shim upgrade be included in this change; current libaio wrapper is on a legacy build. Added dependency note and suggested feature-flag gating for kernel-level io_uring usage.
2026-03-07 — Marco Nguyen: Incorporated async-io shim as optional (feature flag: runtime.feature.handoff_async_io). Local integration tests pass; added canary job config under ci/canary/handoff.yaml.

2026-03-08 — SRE: Ran a 24h canary with 1% traffic; observed no increase in error budget. Telemetry shows handoff queue depth stays < 4 under normal load; transient spikes correlate with GC windows. Request adding lease-transfer histogram to alert set.

2026-03-09 — QA (Priya Singh): Wrote failure-mode tests: simulate rehydration worker crash, simulate slow underlying storage. Verified bounded backpressure prevents admission meltdown; added a regression test to the suite.

2026-03-10 — Marco Nguyen: Merged RFC changes into staging behind feature flag. Next: schedule canary rollout to dedicated cluster on 2026-03-12; follow-up ticket planned for expanding telemetry alerts and docs.
